{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=epistemic+frameworks+for+autonomous+agent+evaluation+of+human-provided+objectives+and+goal-alignment+verification&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7427298\", \"title\": [\"Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Governance (AMEG): Architectural Accountability, Deontic-Epistemic Verification, and Statutory Auditability in Multi-Agent Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>As autonomous multi-agent generative systems transition from conversational prototypes to high-stakes revenue-bearing infrastructure, organizational accountability can no longer rely on extrinsic policy documents audited ex-post. This paper formalizes Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Governance, an architectural runtime framework that embeds institutional governance and statutory mandates directly into the state-transition dynamics of autonomous firms. \\n<br>\\n<br>\\n Extending the Autonomous Micro-Enterprise Architecture state-machine model, it establishes an institutionally regulated eight-tuple combining state spaces, agent actions, transition functions, environmental streams, deontic constraint lattices, settlement primitives, epistemic registries, and execution ledgers. Institutional policies are formalized as a dynamic deontic constraint lattice of obligations, permissions, and prohibitions combined with multi-agent epistemic state tracking, evaluated via a deterministic validation predicate prior to external settlement dispatch. \\n<br>\\n<br>\\n To operationalize the EU AI Act, specifically Title III requirements for high-risk systems under Articles 9, 11, 12, 14, and 15, discrete state mutations are recorded in a cryptographic, tamper-evident Merkle execution tree, guaranteeing mathematical auditability and causal traceability without persisting unbounded natural-language logs. We prove that under a sound normative lattice and bounded self-correction refinement, the probability of an uncontained statutory violation reaching external settlement is analytically bounded. We demonstrate that this framework decouples compliance enforcement from human monitoring payroll while preserving jurisdictional portability across emerging global frameworks.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10…

Functional Emotion and Problem Discovery in Open-ended Artificial Intelligence\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Artificial agents increasingly solve problems, even generating their own goals, once a task or success criterion is available, but what a self-improving system would need to expand its repertoire beyond problems humans have stated remains open. Recent proposals place a frontier before problems are formulated, yet a falsifiable mechanism for this stage, and an argument about whether it requires emotion, are underdeveloped. This paper argues in two stages. First, problem discovery is defined relative to a budget-bounded reachable set, and it is argued that, when the resolving experience is unrelated in content to where an unresolved state arose and verification is scarce, a reliable discoverer must realize three roles: retaining the unresolved state, ranking candidates by a signal that presupposes neither the resolution condition nor content similarity, and funding verification that goal-conditioned utility does not support. Second, it is hypothesized that concern-relative appraisal with directional complementarity realizes this signal and transfers to new concerns and domains, and functional emotion is defined as the assembly that realizes the three roles through an appraisal representation meeting testable criteria. A thought experiment, a comparison of routes and six falsifiable predictions examine the argument…

Given the complexity and variety of situations which post-conflict governments face, (this paper discusses Kosovo, Bosnia, Haiti, and Yugoslavia), there can be no simple rules for implementing transitional justice. Rule of law technical assistance in Haiti was carried out, according to one UNDP advisor, without taking strongly into consideration the key factors that contributed to the deepening of the ongoing political crisis: the lack of capacity, tradition, mechanisms and procedures for the peaceful management and resolution of conflict. Development assistance in the post-conflict rule of law assistance realm should consider revisiting its approach and programming in order to integrate a strong conflict prevention and conflict resolution perspective in  ongoing and planned development cooperation activities.
